name: Papyrus
description: Writing material harvested in the Nile valley and traded from Egypt.
note: Egyptian monopoly represented by the Alexandria production-port anchor

name: Silphium
description: A rare Cyrenaican aromatic and medicinal plant.
note: Barca is a Cyrenaica proxy and the later extinction is reserved for M10

name: Naphtha and Bitumen
description: Natural petroleum and bitumen used as sealant fuel and adhesive.
note: Hit is the source-labelled Mesopotamian bitumen anchor

name: Jade
description: Nephrite prized for carving adornment and exchange along the Tarim routes.
note: Khotan is the direct installed jade anchor

name: Camels
description: Pack camels supporting desert and long-distance overland exchange.
note: Medina is a deliberately narrow Arabian dromedary-trade proxy

name: Olive Oil
description: Pressed and settled olive oil for food lighting bathing ritual and exchange.
note: Creates an exportable Mediterranean processing chain distinct from unpressed olives

name: Salted Fish and Garum
description: Salted fish and fermented fish sauces packed for urban and maritime markets.
note: Combines cetariae products at the market scale without claiming one universal recipe

name: Flour and Bread
description: Milled flour loaves and durable grain preparations supplying towns armies and the annona.
note: Separates processed urban staples from raw grain while keeping the engine food economy legible

name: Perfumes and Unguents
description: Blended aromatic oils resins and unguents for elite ritual and household demand.
note: Supports incense and olive-oil processing as a high-value urban craft

name: Wax Goods
description: Wax tablets seals candles and prepared wax for writing ritual lighting and storage.
note: Connects beeswax to literate civic and household demand

name: Soap and Cleansing Paste
description: Oil ash and mineral cleansing compounds for textile workshops baths and households.
note: Represents varied ancient cleansing compounds without imposing one later standardized recipe

name: Bronze Wares
description: Cast vessels fittings weights bells and domestic objects made from copper and tin.
note: Creates a civilian bronze chain distinct from generic iron tools and weaponry

name: Lead Wares
description: Cast sheets pipes weights clamps and containers made for construction and civic infrastructure.
note: Creates a use for lead in water construction shipping and ordinary fittings

name: Fine Ceramics
description: Fine slipped tablewares lamps and decorated vessels circulated through regional and long-distance markets.
note: Separates high-quality fired wares from ordinary pottery without implying one universal ceramic tradition

name: Glasswares
description: Blown cast and mold-formed glass vessels for household ritual medical and elite use.
note: Represents finished ancient glass vessels rather than raw glass batches

name: Iron Hardware
description: Iron nails chains locks hinges tools and fittings for construction transport and household use.
note: Separates ordinary fabricated ironwork from generic tools and military weaponry

name: Leather Goods
description: Worked sandals straps harnesses scabbards bags and transport fittings made from prepared hides.
note: Represents finished leather manufactures beyond the engine leather intermediate

name: Cordage
description: Twisted plant-fiber rope lines nets and rigging for transport fishing building and shipping.
note: Creates a distinct finished cordage chain used by ancient maritime and land transport

name: Parchment
description: Prepared animal skins cut and finished as durable writing material for archives law and scholarship.
note: Models parchment as a finished writing material alongside geographically bounded papyrus

name: Lacquerware
description: Layered lacquer vessels boxes and fittings made in specialized East Asian workshops.
note: Represents finished Han-period lacquer craft without projecting one court style across all markets

name: Amber Ornaments
description: Drilled polished and mounted amber beads pendants and small ornaments carried through northern exchange routes.
note: Separates worked amber ornaments from raw amber exchange

name: Glass Beads
description: Colored handmade glass beads and small ornaments exchanged across Mediterranean African and Asian networks.
note: Represents portable finished beadwork without assigning every bead assemblage to one production center

name: Woven Carpets
description: Patterned woolen carpets rugs and durable household coverings made on specialized looms.
note: A broad market class for antique woven floor and wall coverings rather than a single later regional style

name: Felt Goods
description: Pressed wool mats caps coverings and practical textiles used across pastoral and settled communities.
note: Separates dense pressed felt manufactures from woven cloth

name: Sailcloth
description: Heavy woven linen and other plant-fiber cloth cut and sewn for ancient sails and maritime maintenance.
note: Creates a distinct maritime textile chain used alongside cordage timber tar and fittings
